// diagnostic

E0508

This map literal writes the key `{key}` twice

What

This map literal writes the key `{key}` twice

Why

A map holds one value per key, so one of the two values would be lost without a word.

Fix

Delete one of the two entries; to replace a value on purpose, assign it after the literal, as in `stats["level"] = 99`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0508: tests/ui/map_literal_duplicate_key.stderr.

Error [jet.MapLiteralDuplicateKey]: This map literal writes the key `"level"` twice
  --> tests/ui/map_literal_duplicate_key.jet:7:40
    |
  7 |     stats := ["level": 3, "score": 10, "level": 7]
    |                                        ^^^^^^^
  --> tests/ui/map_literal_duplicate_key.jet:7:15
    |
  7 |     stats := ["level": 3, "score": 10, "level": 7]
    |               ^^^^^^^ first written here
 Why: A map holds one value per key, so one of the two values would be lost without a word.
 Fix: Delete one of the two entries; to replace a value on purpose, assign it after the literal, as in `stats["level"] = 99`.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0508
